title: United States conducts first airdrop of aid into Gaza
body:
On 2 March 2024, US Central Command announced that US military C-130 cargo aircraft had dropped over 38,000 meals along the coastline of Gaza. The operation was carried out jointly with the Royal Jordanian Air Force. President Joe Biden had announced the airdrops the previous day, after more than 100 Palestinians were reportedly killed in northern Gaza while queuing for aid.

US National Security Council spokesman John Kirby said multiple airdrops would follow over the coming weeks but described them as a supplement to ground deliveries, not a replacement. Israel was allowing only a small amount of aid through the Rafah and Kerem Shalom crossings, with about 2,000 aid trucks reportedly waiting at border crossings, according to analyst Mahjoob Zweiri.

The airdrops were criticised by aid groups. Dave Harden, a former USAID director, called them symbolic and said more land crossings and trucks were needed. Oxfam's Scott Paul described the amount as paltry and symbolic. Medical Aid for Palestinians urged Israel to open all crossings, and the Palestinian Foreign Ministry also criticised the move. Senator Bernie Sanders welcomed it. The war had lasted almost five months at the time.
